transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (NovaEdge Head of ML), Marc Rivera (Platform Eng), Nora Chen (Security), Diego Alvarez (CTO)

Summary:
Quick discovery to scope a Private/VPC deployment for NovaEdge's inference workloads. Main focus: networking (VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway), region constraints (EU/US/AU), key management and audit requirements, and pilot sizing. Agreed next steps and owners at end.

Topics:
- High-level infra & traffic flow
- Cross-account peering and routing
- Private endpoints / interface endpoints / PrivateLink
- Data residency and region constraints (want eu-west-1 + ap-southeast-2 availability)
- KMS/HSM + audit logs + SSO requirements
- Pilot scope and success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intro, i'm Jordan from Redwood, AE for the NovaEdge account, with Samir, our SE — how're you all doing?
[00:05] Aisha: hey, thanks, doing good. we wanted to do a deep pass on networking — we've got a few constraints around region residency and also our security team wants zero public internet egress for inferences.
[00:12] Samir: perfect, that's exactly what we expect to cover. can you describe your current infra? eg where's your training and platform hosted, cloud provider, account layout?
[00:22] Marc: sure — primary infra on AWS, accounts split by environment; prod in account 111111111111, infra tooling in 222222222222. we use a Transit Gateway across accounts, and egress goes through central NAT in prod vpc.
[00:34] Nora: security note — we need all model inference traffic to stay inside our VPCs and peered networks; no public endpoints allowed. KMS keys must be customer-managed, and we need audit logs forwarded to our ELK. also SOC2 compliance is required.
[00:49] Jordan: ok, thanks. two quick clarifications: are you looking at Redwood Dedicated (reserved infra we manage) or Private (our control plane in your VPC / private deployment)?
[00:58] Diego: Private — we want Redwood deployed in our VPCs, control plane with private endpoints inside our accounts. we might later move to Dedicated but initial pilot is Private.
[01:07] Samir: got it. typical topology options: cross-account VPC peering, Transit Gateway attachments, or using AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for control plane egress. each has tradeoffs on management and routing.
[01:20] Aisha: can you explain the differences again? we've got some infra folks but want to understand latency and security tradeoffs.
[01:26] Samir: sure — VPC peering is simple for point-to-point peering but scales poorly at many accounts; Transit Gateway allows hub-and-spoke routing and is good at scale but requires attaching and propagating routes; PrivateLink (interface endpoints) gives you an endpoint service where the Redwood control plane exposes an NLB and you create interface endpoints in your VPC — that keeps traffic private but is region-scoped and adds ENIs.
[01:46] Marc: hm region-scoped is important — we need eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-2 (Australia) active. does PrivateLink work cross-region?
[01:55] Samir: PrivateLink is region-specific. you would need endpoints in each region. Transit Gateway can be used across regions with Transit Gateway inter-region peering, but that can be more complex. for low-latency inference, colocating Redwood workers in the same region as your clients is ideal.
[02:12] Nora: is there any public egress in the Private deployment? we want to ensure no internet paths from inference nodes.
[02:19] Samir: we support fully private deployments where all egress is through your routing (no public internet). our recommendation is to use interface endpoints for the control plane plus Transit Gateway or peering for data plane depending on scale. the inference nodes run in your subnets so you control egress via SGs and route tables.
[02:39] Aisha: ok, how do you handle KV cache and internal model fetching? will nodes contact Redwood's internet endpoints to fetch model shards?
[02:47] Jordan: for Private, model artifacts can be pulled from S3 in your account (we support cross-account roles) or pre-staged in your buckets; alternatively we can pull from our model registry via PrivateLink. Samir, correct me if i'm off.
[02:58] Samir: yep. typical option: push model artifacts to customer S3 and we read via IAM role. if you want us to host model shards, that would be over PrivateLink with appropriate peering and access controls.
[03:10] Marc: we prefer staging in our S3. also curious about IP whitelisting and security groups — what ports and ranges do you need?
[03:18] Samir: we'll share a network guide; generally TCP 443 for control plane endpoints if using PrivateLink, and gRPC or HTTP ports for internal comms (we can confine to 10.x ranges). security groups should allow from your inference subnets to the control plane endpoints.
[03:30] Diego: any requirement for NAT gateway or internet egress for system updates? we try to avoid NAT due to cost and audit.
[03:37] Samir: updates can be fetched via your internal mirrors or S3; no mandatory internet egress. if you do not want NAT, we can operate with interface endpoints and private mirrors.
[03:46] Nora: KMS — we require CMKs for encrypting keys at rest. can Redwood integrate with our CMKs (customer-managed keys) or do you require your own KMS?
[03:55] Samir: we can integrate with customer-managed KMS keys; for Private deployments keys can remain in your account. for Dedicated/hosted we'd use our KMS but can support envelope encryption with your KMS via cross-account grants in some cases.
[04:08] Aisha: what about monitoring and logs? we need audit logs, request traces, and cost/latency metrics forwarded to our systems.
[04:15] Jordan: Redwood Console can push metrics and traces; for Private we can integrate with CloudWatch and forward via cross-account subscriptions or push logs to your ELK — we provide log forwarding hooks and a recommended IAM role.
[04:26] Marc: region constraint: Australia (ap-southeast-2) is important for a subset of clients because of data residency. do you support deploying workers in ap-southeast-2?
[04:35] Samir: yes, we support that region for Private deployments; some GPU instance types are limited there so we'll need to size accordingly. for example, p4d-type GPUs may not be available; we can discuss instance family alternatives (e.g., g5/gn5, or nVIDIA a-series) and quantization to reduce footprint.
[04:52] Aisha: on cost, is there an option to hybridize — control plane in our VPC but use Redwood-managed dedicated GPU pools for burst?
[04:59] Jordan: yes — hybrid is a common pattern: control plane and sensitive workloads in your VPC, and fallback to Redwood Dedicated for burst capacity. routing policies can failover automatically based on SLOs and capacity.
[05:12] Nora: any SLA we should expect on Private?
[05:15] Jordan: SLA depends on the deployment option and contract; for Private we typically offer availability targets in enterprise agreements but operational uptime is jointly owned; we'll include recommended HA patterns (multi-AZ, autoscaling, healthchecks) in the guide.
[05:29] Marc: about cross-account peering: we already use a Transit Gateway for some things; is it simpler to attach Redwood to that vs setting up dedicated peering?
[05:37] Samir: attaching to your Transit Gateway is a good option for scale and central routing. it avoids many peering connections. downside: you'll need route propagation and to ensure security groups and NACLs block any unwanted lateral traffic. private IP addressing and route table design important.
[05:50] Diego: we also have an on-prem datacenter with Direct Connect; can Redwood route traffic over DX to the Private deployment?
[05:58] Samir: yes — since the nodes are in your VPCs, they can be reached from on-prem over DX as long as routing and TGW/peering is configured. we recommend testing bandwidth and latency for inference workloads.
[06:10] Aisha: what's the minimum pilot size you recommend? we want a realistic costing and performance baseline.
[06:15] Samir: for a pilot we usually recommend 1-2 worker nodes (GPUs) per region matching your inference QPS; e.g., if you expect 20qps with 500 token avg per request, that maps to X tokens/sec; we'll help size. typical pilot is 2-4 GPUs across eu-west-1 + ap-southeast-2.
[06:34] Marc: any specific networking tests we should run?
[06:37] Samir: yes — ping/iperf for latency/bandwidth, and a mock inference load to measure end-to-end latency including KV cache warm-up. we'll provide a benchmark harness.
[06:48] Jordan: quick note — i'll send sample terraform and a network checklist. Samir will follow up with deep-dive scheduling.
[06:55] Nora: also would like to see how authentication works — SSO, SAML, RBAC mapping to our IdP.
[07:02] Samir: for Private we integrate with customer SSO via SAML/OIDC; admin roles can be mapped to your IdP groups. we also support fine-grained RBAC for routes and models. we'll document the mapping steps and provide a sample SAML metadata file.
[07:16] Aisha: are there any known gotchas with AWS PrivateLink and SGs? we've hit ENI limits in past projects.
[07:22] Samir: yes ENI limits exist per AZ per account; for big fleets we recommend using Transit Gateway or request quota increases. PrivateLink also requires interface endpoints in each AZ, which can increase cost. we'll include cost estimates.
[07:36] Marc: and what about service discovery / DNS — do you rely on private hosted zones?
[07:42] Samir: we typically recommend Private Hosted Zones with resolver rules if you want short hostnames; otherwise you can use the VPC endpoint DNS names. if cross-account, resolver rules or Route53 resolver rules are needed.
[07:53] Jordan: quick recapping: customer wants Private deployment, no public egress, CMK in customer account, audit logs to ELK, support for eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-2, and prefer S3-staged models. next steps: we share guides and schedule deep dive.
[08:05] Aisha: yes that's right. also timeframe: we're aiming for a pilot by end of Q2, legal needs to review security docs earlier.
[08:12] Jordan: understood. we'll get SOC2 + security pack over.
[08:18] Marc: couple of clarifying Qs — how do you handle model updates without exposing endpoints?
[08:23] Samir: model updates can be pushed by you to S3 and we pull via role, or via an artifact pipeline within your VPC. no internet-facing pulls required. for cases where we host models, we'd use PrivateLink to pull from our registry.
[08:36] Diego: are there any performance differences if we use PrivateLink vs TGW?
[08:41] Samir: PrivateLink tends to be simpler for control plane traffic; TGW is better for high-volume data plane. latency differences are usually small within region; cross-region TGW peering adds latency. for tight p50/p95 latency SLAs, collocate workers in region and use local routing.
[08:58] Aisha: can you do per-route VPC flow logs for auditing?
[09:03] Samir: VPC Flow Logs can be enabled and forwarded to your ELK; we can also hook request logs from the runtime into your logging pipeline.
[09:12] Marc: about encryption in transit — do you rely on mTLS between control plane and nodes?
[09:18] Samir: yes, we support mTLS within the cluster for node-node and node-control communications; certificates can be managed by us or integrated with your PKI.
[09:29] Jordan: any legal procurement comment from Diego?
[09:32] Diego: procurement will ask for DPA and security addendum; legal will need SOC2 report. depending on where we host keys, might need additional contract language.
[09:44] Jordan: we'll send standard DPA and security materials.
[09:47] Aisha: excellent. anything else on routing policies?
[09:51] Samir: one more note: we can set smart routing policies to prefer local region workers and fallback to Redwood Dedicated in emergencies; these policies live in the deployment config.
[10:03] Marc: on quotas and ENI limits, we'll loop in our infra team to see if we need quota increases.
[10:09] Jordan: ok let's talk about pilot success criteria — what must be true for pilot success?
[10:14] Aisha: we want sub-200ms p95 for standard prompts in eu-west-1, no public egress, CMK encryption, and logs flowing to ELK. cost per 1k tokens under our target (we'll provide target).
[10:25] Samir: great. we'll collaborate on sizing and provide benchmark harness.
[10:30] Nora: can you show the network diagram in the deep-dive? that's crucial.
[10:34] Samir: yes i'll present a diagram showing VPCs, TGW, PrivateLink endpoints, route tables and SGs.
[10:40] Jordan: last thing — any competitor details we should be aware of?
[10:43] Diego: we've talked to Anthropic and AWS SageMaker team; Anthropic pitched hosted-only, SageMaker has managed endpoints but ops cost was high. we wanted Redwood because of the private deploy option.
[10:55] Jordan: understood. ok we'll prioritize the security docs and network guide. thanks everyone.

(brief wrap / recap)
[11:05] Jordan: recap and owners — action items reviewed (see email). we'll follow up with the docs and schedule deep-dive.
[11:12] Aisha: thanks, bye.
[11:15] meeting end
